THE MUSIC_GRAPH OUTSTANDING LIST, CHECKED AGAINST THE RUNNING BUILD RATHER THAN AGAINST THE PREVIOUS TRIAGE NOTE — which is the rule `fact:the-music-graph-feedback-file-is-four-sessions-and-its-first-batch-was-fixed-long-ago` yielded and this is its first application.

⭐ TWO PRIOR RECORDS FROM 2026-08-16 DISAGREE WITH EACH OTHER, and noticing that is why this was re-checked. `fact:feedback-triage-status-across-three-sources-2026-08-16` lists F6 and F7 as "confirmed already covered"; `fact:the-music-graph-feedback-file-is-four-sessions...` lists F6 and F7 as "NOT YET VERIFIED". Same day, same corpus, opposite claims. Neither is obviously wrong and the conflict itself is the finding: a to-do list about feedback drifts exactly like any other uncomputed record.

CLOSED SINCE THE LAST TRIAGE (verified today):
• F10 (`coverage_report` calls a swept file unobserved when a parent directory also claims it) — FIXED by PR #218, `chg:a-claim-is-not-hidden-by-its-parent`. It was on the open list and closed four days after that list was written.

REPRODUCED, STILL OPEN:
• F8 (`export_graph` will not create its own parent directory) — REPRODUCED LIVE 2026-08-17. Exporting to a path with a missing parent fails with "No such file or directory (os error 2)". Partially improved since the report: the message now names the path. It still does not say the parent is missing, nor that one mkdir fixes it, and the reporter's point stands — AGENTS.md documents a restore path (`.reflow2/backups/`) that does not exist in a fresh design, so the instructions name the path the tool rejects.

NOT TESTABLE FROM AN MCP CLIENT, honestly recorded as unverified rather than guessed:
• F17 (`get_node`'s argument error takes two round trips; neither message names both required fields) — the harness validates arguments against the tool schema before they reach reflow2, so the wrong-argument path cannot be exercised from here. Needs a raw JSON-RPC probe (`tools/smoke_mcp.py` is the place). The reporter measured it at EIGHT TOOL CALLS, so it is worth the probe.

LIKELY ADDRESSED, NOT YET CONFIRMED AGAINST THE REPORTER'S EXACT CASE:
• F19 (`what_next` hides most of the open set with no way to page) — the tool NOW ACCEPTS `limit`, which is one of the two things the reporter asked for, and reports `not_shown` and `unranked_pool`. Whether that satisfies them is not established.
• F18 (gap-acknowledgement Decisions swamp real Decisions) — `what_next` states "Review records excluded throughout" and `structure.rs` keeps `decision:ack:` ids out of the design network (BL-124). But the reporter's actual complaint was about `scan_nodes {node_type: Decision, brief: true}` returning 41 bookkeeping rows of 71, and that read path was not checked today.
• F20 ("Delivered: 10 of 21 (20 satisfied)" reads as a contradiction) — the report now carries an explanatory clause ("computed from the thread ... not from a status field"), which is weaker than the reporter's ask to name both numbers plainly. Judgement, not a defect.

OPEN AND UNCHECKED TODAY: F6, F7 (see the disagreement above), F9, F13, F14, F15.
• F9 and F14 are the same shape and are the most interesting of the remainder: recording planned work MANUFACTURES gaps (unrealized/unverified per planned capability), so the gap list punishes writing a plan down, and one detector can bury every other finding. That is `req:a-deliberate-state-is-not-a-defect` (accepted) arriving from a third direction, and it may already be covered by that requirement rather than needing its own.
• F15 (running `reconcile_artifacts` does not clear the loop_status item it tells you to run) — the count is now 1 rather than the reporter's 27, but whether the underlying non-clearing behaviour is fixed was not established.
• F13 (`unmotivated_capability` misreports provenance in its evidence string) — a report stating something the node does not say, which is squarely this increment's theme and was not checked.
